Draft MOU and partner onboarding checklist
action_items: Maya: Send partner deck + pricing links by 2026-10-18
Ethan: Prepare rough benchmark plan for 1 GPU and 4 GPU configs by 2026-10-22

header:
Date: 2026-10-16
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Kaur (Redwood Partnerships); Oliver Grant, Nina Soto, Derek Han, Spenser Li (Coastline GPU)
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and Coastline GPU to explore reseller/integration partnership. Discussed product fit, typical customer workloads (inference for LLMs), deployment models (hosted, dedicated, private/VPC), security/compliance expectations, and next steps for a technical pilot and MOU.
topics: Redwood Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
questions: What are Coastline's most common customer SLAs?
How does Coastline handle multi-tenant isolation on shared racks?
Any regional data residency constraints we should know?
What level of co-marketing/support is expected in the early pilot?
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're excited to learn more about Coastline and see where Redwood could fit. Quick intros?
[00:09] Oliver Grant: Hi all, I'm Oliver, Head of Partnerships at Coastline GPU. Welcome.
[00:12] Nina Soto: Nina, solutions architect, I mostly look after the inference and orchestration side.
[00:16] Derek Han: Derek, bizdev.
[00:18] Spenser Li: Spenser, infra engineer, I manage the fleet.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Great. Ethan and I are from Redwood, Ethan's our SE.
[00:25] Ethan Rivera: Hey, hi, thanks. Quick agenda — partner model, technical fit, security, then next steps. Sound OK?
[00:31] Oliver Grant: Yup. High level, we've got hyperscale racks with custom cooling, we've been packaging them as an OEM solution for cloud partners and want to expand into the LLM inference stack.
[00:41] Nina Soto: A lot of our customers are looking for low-latency inference — real-time chat, multi-tenant SaaS. They ask about batching, KV cache behavior, and SLOs.
[00:50] Ethan Rivera: That's right up Redwood's alley. We support hosted, dedicated, and private/VPC models. For partners doing on-prem or co-located, our Private deployment can run behind customer-controlled networking and KMS.
[01:03] Spenser Li: Quick question — do you need any special kernel patches for our card firmware? We run mixed Ampere and next-gen custom designs.
[01:10] Ethan Rivera: We have a kernel/compilation layer that selects optimized kernels based on architecture; there are edge cases but usually we can support via a short onboarding and a small compatibility shim. Occasionally we have quirks with custom drivers — we've seen that with some specialized NV switches — but that's solvable.
[01:28] Nina Soto: When you say "dedicated" what's the isolation? Are we talking reserved GPUs per customer or multi-tenant with software isolation?
[01:35] Maya Chen: Both models are possible. Dedicated means reserved pools and predictable throughput — good for higher SLAs — while hosted multi-tenant is cheaper. For partners reselling hardware, Dedicated instances map nicely to reserved racks.
[01:46] Derek Han: Commercially, are there resell margins or marketplace programs?
[01:50] Maya Chen: We have partner tiers — resale/managed partners get different pricing and co-marketing. Priya can follow up with the partner program doc.
[01:57] Priya Kaur: Yep I'll share the one-pager and enablement checklist.
[02:01] Oliver Grant: Security huge for our customers. SOC2 is a must, plus SAML/SSO integration, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration for keys.
[02:10] Ethan Rivera: Redwood is SOC2 Type II, supports SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments. For hosted, we also provide customer-managed keys in some enterprise plans. We'll share the security pack.
[02:23] Nina Soto: Do you have examples of latency numbers for 8k context with 2k output on Llama-like models? We want to compare to customers that use optimized stacks.
[02:31] Ethan Rivera: Ballpark depends on quantization and model. For a 13B open model, on an A100-class instance in Dedicated, p50 token latency in our infra is sub-50ms for short responses — but for long context sizes it grows, obviously. We'll propose a benchmark matrix for 1-GPU and 4-GPU configs.
[02:48] Spenser Li: Also what's your approach to KV cache caching and cross-request reuse?
[02:52] Ethan Rivera: We do prefix and KV cache reuse heuristics and we can enable workload-aware batching. There's also an option for local cache tiers on the host to reduce repeated token compute.
[03:03] Oliver Grant: From a go-to-market lens, we can bundle Redwood as an option for customers who want a higher-level managed inference runtime on our gear. How would support and SLAs look?
[03:12] Maya Chen: For Dedicated/reserved we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, and a premium support tier for faster incident response. For partner resales we have enablement and a joint support playbook.
[03:22] Derek Han: Any objections we've seen from previous partners?
[03:25] Ethan Rivera: Common ones — price sensitivity vs latency, and concerns about data residency. We address with routing policies and private deployments. Also some partners want white-labeling and that's on the table depending on contract.
[03:37] Nina Soto: For pilots, we like short proofs — 4-week pilot with defined workloads. Can you run a pilot that uses our hardware in a co-located setup?
[03:45] Ethan Rivera: Yes, that's feasible. Typical pilot: deploy Private control plane, run 2-4 models, collect perf/cost metrics, iterate. We'll need infra diagrams, firewall rules, and a signed NDA/MOU.
[03:55] Oliver Grant: On the technical side, our edge boxes also have an M.2 cache tier — would Redwood be able to use local NVMe for caching?
[04:02] Ethan Rivera: Absolutely, we can configure local disk caches for model artifacts and KV cache layers. We'll need to validate IO patterns during the deep-dive.
[04:11] Spenser Li: Anything special about orchestration? We generally run Nomad + custom scheduler; customers sometimes use K8s.
[04:18] Ethan Rivera: Redwood runtime can be deployed on K8s or on bare-metal orchestrated stacks; there are Kubernetes operators we've used but Nomad is less common — we'd want to do an integration session.
[04:29] Maya Chen: Let's talk commercial mapping. If Coastline bundles Redwood as an option, we'd do either revenue share or resale pricing per capacity commit. There are also reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated.
[04:40] Derek Han: For pricing — do you have a partner discount schedule?
[04:43] Priya Kaur: We do, I'll include partner discount tiers and recommended pilot pricing in the follow-up.
[04:48] Oliver Grant: Great. A couple of specific asks: can you share a benchmark plan and a sample MOU? Also we need SOC2 and encryption docs for our procurement.
[04:57] Maya Chen: Yep, next steps captured. We'll send the partner deck, security pack, and a draft MOU. For the benchmark plan Ethan will lay out a 1-GPU and 4-GPU plan.
[05:06] Nina Soto: Timeline — we'd like to get a pilot started in November, ideally second week.
[05:10] Maya Chen: That sounds workable; we'll aim to have materials and a proposed pilot schedule by Oct 22.
[05:14] Oliver Grant: One more — any limits on model licenses? Are you comfortable with partners running open models and customer-provided weights?
[05:20] Ethan Rivera: We support open models and customer-provided weights. For licensed models we enforce the vendor terms — typically that's fine for Private deployments. We'll include licensing notes.
[05:30] Derek Han: Competitors — our customers sometimes eval with NVIDIA's software stack and smaller players like Lambda Labs.
[05:34] Maya Chen: Understood. Redwood focuses on serving economics and operational predictability as differentiation.
[05:40] Priya Kaur: I'll follow up on co-marketing possibilities and partner enablement.
[05:44] Oliver Grant: Cool. Anything else from your side?
[05:46] Spenser Li: Not from me.
[05:47] Nina Soto: No.
[05:48] Maya Chen: Closing recap — send partner one-pager + pricing, security pack, draft MOU, infra diagram request, and schedule SE deep-dive for benchmarks.
[05:58] Oliver Grant: Thanks all.
[06:00] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[44:30] Meeting end (note: timestamps after 06:00 are wall-clock placeholders to reflect full 45m duration).

Notes: transcript has minor auto-transcription noise; proper nouns sometimes abbreviated (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cache"). Shared artifacts mentioned during call: partner-deck link (https://redwood.example.com/partners/coastline-deck), security-pack link (https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-pack), benchmark-template (Google Sheet link shared in chat).
